clue.text: Around noon, bad dealer shot conductor

indicators.note: the word bad goes around the letter for noon, enclosing it
shot in the sense of ruined or wrecked, so the letters of dealer are rearranged

explanation.surface: At midday a hopeless card dealer opens fire on a conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' is the anagram signal, in its sense of ruined, and applies only to 'dealer'; 'Around' wraps the first word round N.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandleader directs a band, so is a kind of conductor of musicians.

clue.text: Outlaw sex? Led Zeppelin perhaps not behind that!

indicators.note: says the band does not come after the other piece, so it is placed in front

parts.note: Led Zeppelin is an example of a rock band
IT is a long-standing euphemism for sex

explanation.surface: A joke about Led Zeppelin's rock-star lifestyle: hardly behind the times on sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not behind that' is a placement signal: the group goes in front of the euphemism for sex rather than after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber living outside the law, so an outlaw.

clue.text: Sacred as Jesus' hands, as people have told us

indicators.note: what people have told us is something heard spoken, signalling a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Jesus' hands were pierced by nails at the crucifixion, so they were holey, full of holes

explanation.surface: A statement about Jesus being sacred, as we have been told by others.
explanation.walkthrough: HOLEY (full of holes) and HOLY are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy and sacred are synonyms, both meaning set apart and dedicated to God.

clue.text: Do this and engineer penury and a touch of depression

definitions.text: Do this and engineer penury and a touch of depression

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or construct, so the letters of penury, a and the extra letter are reworked
only a touch, the first letter, of the word depression is used

explanation.surface: Pay workers too little and you bring about poverty and some gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineer' shuffles PENURY plus A plus D, the first letter that 'a touch of' takes from 'depression'. The whole clue also describes what underpaying someone does.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying staff too little causes poverty and low spirits, which the whole clue describes as the result of the act.

clue.text: Unemployed Hoskins had beer, but no starter

parts.note: the setter Hoskins, speaking as I, would say I'd for I had

indicators.note: the starter, the first letter, of the beer word is dropped

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: The setter, out of work, drank beer but skipped the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoskins is the setter, so 'Hoskins had' is I'D. 'no starter' removes the A from ALE to leave LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can describe someone without work, so it is a synonym of unemployed.

clue.text: A daughter enthralled by hired killer's swagger

indicators.note: being enthralled by something is being held within it, so these letters sit inside

parts.note: a bravo is an old word for a hired assassin

explanation.surface: A girl is captivated by a contract killer's cocky manner.
explanation.walkthrough: A bravo, from Italian, is a hired thug or assassin, not the cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a showy display of boldness, which is what swagger means.

clue.text: Man of intellect lowering head to another

indicators.note: in a down entry, lowering a letter moves it further down the word

parts.note: brain is a common word for intellect

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, of the word another names the letter to move

explanation.surface: A clever man demotes his leader in favour of someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The head of 'another' is A; 'lowering' it in BRAIN, a down answer, moves it below the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian is a common man's first name, the kind of example a bare man stands for in crosswords.

clue.text: Jog naked around the centre of Rugby

indicators.note: the naked word goes around the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: nude means naked

indicators.note: the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter

explanation.surface: A streaker runs naked across the middle of a Rugby pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jog' looks like a run but is the verb to nudge. 'the centre of' Rugby is G.
explanation.definitionFit: To jog someone's elbow is to nudge it, a gentle push.

clue.text: On removing their tops, flirt and aristo quieten down

indicators.note: their tops are the first letters of both words, which are taken away

parts.note: a tease is a flirt who leads others on
a toff is British slang for an upper-class person, an aristocrat

explanation.surface: A flirt and a toff strip off their tops and then calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On removing their tops' drops the first T from TEASE and from TOFF, leaving EASE and OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off is to lessen in intensity, an idiom meaning to calm or quieten down.

clue.text: Emissions from SEAT and Triumph 500

parts.note: to triumph is to win
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Exhaust fumes from cars made by SEAT and Triumph, two motor makers.
explanation.walkthrough: SEAT and Triumph look like car brands, but seat is the backside, and wind is gas emitted from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind is flatulence, gas passed from the backside you sit on.

clue.text: Period of time in which duke meets lady occasionally

indicators.note: taking letters only now and then means every other letter of the word lady

explanation.surface: A spell during which a nobleman sometimes meets a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes every other letter of lady, A and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A day is a span of twenty-four hours, a common unit of time.

clue.text: Flat seas and oceans primarily will be still

parts.note: even means flat or level

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the opening letters of both words are taken

explanation.surface: A forecast: calm seas and oceans will be motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like the calm sea, but is the adverb meaning nevertheless.
explanation.definitionFit: Even so and still both mean nevertheless, despite what has just been said.

clue.text: Current news at the front? Two rude fools about to hug!

indicators.note: hugging something is wrapping around it, so the letter goes inside
fooling about is messing around, so the letters of two rude are jumbled
the letter at the front of the word news is its first

explanation.surface: A headline about two rude idiots about to embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fools about' rearranges TWO RUDE, and 'to hug' puts N, the front of 'news', inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertow is a current beneath the surface of the sea flowing away from the shore.

clue.text: With a bit of luck, head of Kew Society gets acquitted

indicators.note: only a bit, the first letter, of the word luck is used
the head of each of the words Kew and Society is its first letter

explanation.surface: If lucky, the head of the Kew Society, a gardening body, escapes conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walks' is slang, chiefly American, for being acquitted and walking free from court.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk is slang for being cleared of a charge and leaving court free.

clue.text: Super-happy thong covers up Serpent

indicators.note: the words cover up letters within them, which are taken out across the two words

explanation.surface: An over-cheerful thong conceals a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Super-happy' into 'thong'.
explanation.definitionFit: A python is a large constricting snake, so a kind of serpent.

clue.text: Surprisingly, claimant is bringing good luck

indicators.note: said of an unexpected turn, telling us the letters of claimant is come out in a surprising order

explanation.surface: A claimant unexpectedly proves lucky.
explanation.definitionFit: A talismanic object works like a charm, believed to bring its owner fortune.

clue.text: Drug-smuggling old man in Six Feet Under?

indicators.note: smuggling means carrying something hidden inside, so the drug letter sits within

parts.note: old man is slang for father, dad
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A storyline from the TV drama Six Feet Under, about an old man smuggling drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Six Feet Under is an American TV drama about undertakers; buried six feet under, you are dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone six feet under is buried in a grave, so is no longer living.

clue.text: Removing a rat is beneath Her Maj

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece beneath another comes after it

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen, Her Majesty
to rat on someone is to sing, informing on them

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a rat is beneath the Queen's dignity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rat' is the verb to inform, as is 'sing'. 'is beneath' places A SING under ER in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasing something wipes it out, so is a way of removing it.

clue.text: Kid is one making bishop look small and stupid

indicators.note: making one thing look like another turns it into it, so one letter is swapped for another
with making, says the bishop letter is turned into the small letter

parts.note: Billy the Kid, the outlaw, is one Billy
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A child who makes a bishop seem small and foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' wants to be a child, but it points to Billy the Kid, a famous Wild West gunman; replace its B with S.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly and stupid are near-synonyms, both meaning foolish or lacking sense.

clue.text: Bags of cash? Let's let loose!

indicators.note: letting the letters loose frees them to form a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cry to throw money bags around wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: Satchels are bags carried on the shoulder, typically schoolbags.

clue.text: Story written about France in US magazine

indicators.note: written round something, so the story word encloses the letter

parts.note: a story is a lie, an untruth
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: An article on France published in an American magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Story' and 'written about' look like journalism; the story is a fib, LIE, around F.
explanation.definitionFit: Life was a famous American picture magazine of news and photojournalism.

clue.text: One who is likely to repeat usual rubbish

definitions.text: One who is likely to repeat

parts.note: par is the usual or normal standard, as in par for the course
rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone who will repeat the usual nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A parrot is a bird that mimics speech, and by extension a person who copies others.

clue.text: Southern females must change, to be exact

indicators.note: the word females has to change its letter order

explanation.surface: Women from the South have to alter in order to be precise.
explanation.definitionFit: Selfsame means the very same, identical, so exact in the sense of the exact one.

clue.text: Don't start song after bit of lovely junk

indicators.note: the trimmed song comes after the bit of lovely
a bit of the word lovely is its first letter
the song word does not start, losing its first letter

parts.note: a number is a song in a performance

explanation.surface: A plea not to strike up a song after some lovely rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start' drops N from NUMBER to leave UMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumber in British use is unwanted old furniture and other clutter, so junk.

clue.text: Boy, 10 today, getting disheartened

parts.note: 10 refers to the answer at 10-across, DAY, and Mon, short for Monday, is a day

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letters of the word today go

explanation.surface: A boy celebrating his tenth birthday today gets upset.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like an age but points to the answer DAY, of which MON is one. 'getting disheartened' strips TODAY to TY.
explanation.definitionFit: Monty is a man's first name, so a boy in the crossword sense of a male name.

clue.text: Equipment found by small children's camp?

parts.note: kit is gear or equipment
CH is the abbreviation for children

explanation.surface: Gear turned up beside a little one's summer camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camp' wants to be the holiday camp of the surface; it is the adjective for tasteless, showy style.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp taste and kitsch both describe deliberately showy, tasteless style; the question mark marks it as an example.

clue.text: Secretary into S&M gets unwanted mail

indicators.note: being into something can mean being inside it, so these letters go within

parts.note: S&M, sadomasochism, gives the letters S and M
a PA, personal assistant, is a secretary

explanation.surface: An office secretary who is into kinky sex receives junk mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' looks like 'keen on' in the surface, but is a placement signal for putting one piece inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is unsolicited bulk email, so unwanted electronic post.

clue.text: Impromptu session in the morning after joint

indicators.note: the morning letters come after the joint letter

parts.note: J is slang for a cannabis joint
AM stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: An unplanned music session in the morning following a joint of cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam is an improvised get-together of musicians playing without rehearsal.

clue.text: Sailor one associated with bowls?

definitions.meaning: ..., or ... tar, is an old name for a sailor
in lawn bowls the ... is the small target ball the players aim at

explanation.surface: A sailor known for his bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack is a traditional nickname for a seaman and the white target ball in the game of bowls.

clue.text: Relative is wasted being out of head

indicators.note: the word is without its head, its first letter

parts.note: gaunt means thin and wasted

explanation.surface: A relative is drunk and out of their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' and 'out of head' look like drunkenness; wasted is GAUNT, and losing its head drops the G.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a parent's sister, a family relative.

clue.text: Girl having trouble eating rare platter

indicators.note: eating something takes it in, so the rare letter goes inside

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for girl
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A girl struggling to eat a rare steak from a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having trouble' looks like an anagram signal; 'having' joins G to AIL. R goes after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy Grail is the legendary dish or cup of the Last Supper, so a platter.

clue.text: Relics broken by half-cut Oxbridge fellows?

indicators.note: something broken comes apart, so the letters of relics are rearranged
the word by cut in half keeps only its second letter

explanation.surface: Holy relics smashed by tipsy Oxford and Cambridge dons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' looks like drunk, but halves 'by' to its last letter, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The clerisy are scholars and intellectuals as a class; Oxbridge dons are an example, hence the question mark.
